program_meta.advisor_model: APPLY TO THE PROGRAMME, NOT TO AN ADVISOR -- admission is a single, centralized MSc CS admission decision with no named-supervisor requirement (this is the OPPOSITE of the Direct Doctorate track, which DOES require identifying two preferred research groups in the motivation letter). Confirmed by direct evidence from multiple ETH research groups' own thesis/student-project pages (all read directly): Prof. A. Krause's Learning & Adaptive Systems (LAS) group states, VERBATIM: 'If you are interested in working with us, you can send an application... Make sure that your email includes: a résumé, a recent transcript of records, your intended start date, and we highly recommend that you mention the projects you are interested in, members of the group with whom you would like to work, or recent publications by the group relevant to your interests.' Prof. M. Pollefeys's Computer Vision and Geometry Group (CVG), VERBATIM: 'We are always looking for students pursuing master/bachelor/semester theses with us... If you are interested in a particular topic, have a look at the pages of our group members... and contact the respective researcher directly.' Prof. G. Rätsch's Biomedical Informatics Group (BMI), VERBATIM: 'The BMI lab accepts motivated students to carry out their bachelor and master thesis research in the group... contact us if you are interested,' with instructions to use '#application #info' in the subject line. NET EFFECT for cold-email strategy: unlike UT Austin/Berkeley-style 'do not contact faculty before admission' norms, at ETH the entire semester-project/thesis placement mechanism IS direct, individual contact with a professor or their PhD students/postdocs -- but this happens AFTER MSc admission, once enrolled, when selecting each semester's project or the final MSc thesis. There is no verified ETH-wide policy statement that explicitly frames 'master's students as co-authors/real researchers' in so many words within the pages read this pass (the 'Master's as researcher' culture is inferred from the mechanics of the semester-project system -- 1-2 projects per semester, each placed directly in a professor's research group working alongside PhD students, several explicitly producing conference-venue publications, e.g. LAS's page: 'M.Sc. projects at LAS often result in publications at leading conferences,' with multiple named ETH-Medal-winning student theses published at NeurIPS/ICLR/AISTATS/UAI -- rather than from an explicit official quote naming that framing). GAP: no single official ETH/D-INFK page was found asserting the 'master's-as-researcher' culture in verbatim terms; the evidence here is structural (the LAS/CVG/BMI examples) rather than a single citable policy quote.
program_meta.ms_research_access: Yes, and this is the central mechanism of the ETH MSc, not an optional add-on. The Master in Computer Science requires Semester Projects and a Master's thesis as core, credit-bearing components, each placed in a specific ETH research group. The department's own theses page (inf.ethz.ch/studies/semester-and-master-theses.html) is literally organized as a directory of every ETH-CS-affiliated research group with a direct link to that group's own thesis-topics page (e.g., LAS: https://las.inf.ethz.ch/teaching/student-projects; CVG: https://cvg.ethz.ch/opportunities/; BMI: https://bmi.inf.ethz.ch/opportunities/; MDS/Vogt: https://mds.inf.ethz.ch/opportunities/). LAS explicitly notes: 'M.Sc. projects at LAS often result in publications at leading conferences,' with a long list of ETH-Medal-winning master's theses that became first-author NeurIPS/ICLR/AISTATS/UAI papers -- direct, verifiable evidence of the 'master's students as real researchers/co-authors' culture the user flagged.

faculty.department: Department of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering (D-ITET) -- Computer Vision Lab
faculty.research_areas: Computational methods for analysing medical images: segmentation, anomaly detection, uncertainty quantification, and learning from disparately labeled/weakly labeled clinical data (brain MRI, surgical instrument tracking).
faculty.why_match: Akshat's DDPM-pretraining study found that a frozen diffusion encoder retains >80% of fully fine-tuned liver-segmentation Dice but performs WORSE than random initialization on kidney -- an unresolved, organ-dependent negative result about when a learned unsupervised prior actually transfers. Konukoglu's group's 2025 MICCAI paper 'Anomaly Detection by Clustering DINO Embeddings using a Dirichlet Process Mixture' (Schulthess et al.) is built on exactly the same premise Akshat is probing -- that a frozen, pretrained embedding space is only USEFULLY structured for some anatomical/pathological targets and not others, and the group has to explicitly model that heterogeneity (via a Dirichlet Process mixture) rather than assume it away. The group's MedIA 2025 paper 'Learning to segment anatomy and lesions from disparately labeled sources in brain MRI' (Himmetoglu et al.) is directly in Akshat's label-scarcity thread (interest B/C): learning from labels that are inconsistent/partial across data sources is the structural cousin of his own pseudo-label-filtering and diffusion-pretraining-under-scarce-labels work.
faculty.key_paper_1: Anomaly Detection by Clustering DINO Embeddings using a Dirichlet Process Mixture. Y. Zhou, N. Schulthess, et al. MICCAI, 2025.
faculty.key_paper_2: Learning to segment anatomy and lesions from disparately labeled sources in brain MRI. M. Himmetoglu, et al. Medical Image Analysis, 2025.

faculty.research_areas: Statistical machine learning under uncertainty: Gaussian processes and Bayesian deep learning, active learning, bandits and sequential decision-making, safe/robust reinforcement learning, Bayesian optimization, causal structure learning, large-scale/online learning.
faculty.why_match: Akshat's semi-supervised spine-MRI work directly compared MC-dropout uncertainty against confidence thresholding for filtering pseudo-labels and found the two give equivalent pseudo-label quality (combining them added nothing), while per-class thresholds calibrated on just 5 reference images matched those derived from 304 -- a concrete empirical result about how much labelled calibration data an uncertainty-driven selection rule actually needs. LAS's flagship recent result, 'Transductive Active Learning: Theory and Applications' (Hübotter et al., NeurIPS 2024, ETH Medal), is the theory-grade version of that exact question: how to select which unlabeled points are worth acquiring/using, with formal guarantees rather than Akshat's hand-tuned per-class thresholds. LAS's active general-areas listing explicitly includes 'Active Learning' and 'Probabilistic Approaches (Gaussian processes, Bayesian Deep Learning)' as ongoing project categories, directly overlapping interest (B).
faculty.key_paper_1: Transductive Active Learning: Theory and Applications. J. Hübotter, B. Sukhija, L. Treven, Y. As, A. Krause. NeurIPS, 2024 (Awarded ETH Medal).
faculty.key_paper_2: Neural Contextual Bandits without Regret. P. Kassraie, A. Krause. AISTATS, 2022. (See also LAS's active 2026 topic 'Sequential Confidence Estimation via Likelihood Mixing' -- online convex optimization, confidence sets, frequentist/Bayesian statistics.)

faculty.research_areas: Machine learning for medical/healthcare data: interpretable and concept-based models (concept bottleneck models), multi-view learning, representation learning for clinical/ultrasound/bio-signal data, discovering and removing hidden biases in learned representations.
faculty.why_match: Akshat's A-PDF work built a hand-designed, distribution-based plausibility filter to catch GAN-generated masks whose class-proportions don't match the real-data distribution -- i.e., a mechanism for detecting when a learned model's outputs are silently wrong in a way a discriminator alone would miss. Vogt's group's ETH-Medal-winning master's thesis 'Interpretable Approach to Discover and Remove Hidden Biases' (Vandenhirtz, with Manduchi and Marcinkevics) is the general, principled version of exactly that concern -- finding and removing a hidden, spurious signal a model has learned, rather than trusting its outputs at face value. Her group's other flagship thesis, 'Multi-View Concept Bottleneck Models on Ultrasound Data for Pediatric Appendicitis' (Klimiene, also ETH Medal), is squarely in interest (D)/(E): structured, constrained prediction (concept bottlenecks are an explicit structural constraint on what the model is allowed to use, analogous to HiME's chain-rule structural constraint) applied to real clinical imaging data.
faculty.key_paper_1: Interpretable Approach to Discover and Remove Hidden Biases. M. Vandenhirtz, L. Manduchi, R. Marcinkevics, J. E. Vogt. (Master's thesis / associated publication; OpenReview, cited via MDS Opportunities page.)
faculty.key_paper_2: Multi-View Concept Bottleneck Models on Ultrasound Data for Pediatric Appendicitis. U. Klimiene, R. Marcinkevics, E. Özkan Elsen, J. E. Vogt. (Interpretable ML in Healthcare Workshop, 2022; Awarded ETH Medal.)

faculty.department: Department of Computer Science (D-INFK) -- Institute of Visual Computing
faculty.lab: Computer Vision and Learning (VLG) Group, https://vlg.inf.ethz.ch/
faculty.research_areas: 3D human modelling and generative models for digital humans: human motion/shape generation, human-scene interaction, video understanding, generative modelling of articulated/structured visual data.
faculty.why_match: HiME's central contribution is a decoding rule that turns per-level conditional sigmoids into a provably-consistent, upward-closed prediction set over a fixed hierarchical taxonomy (Galaxy Zoo 2's 4-level, 37-class structure) -- a guarantee about STRUCTURED, hierarchically-constrained output spaces, obtained cheaply (~0.01% parameter overhead) rather than via heavy post-hoc correction. Tang's 'Digital Humans' research programme works on exactly the harder version of that problem: a human body/motion is itself an extremely constrained hierarchical/kinematic structure (joints nested under limbs nested under a root), and her group's generative models for human motion and human-scene interaction must respect that same kind of structural consistency by construction, not by post-processing, in a domain far more complex than Akshat's classification taxonomy.
